name: Learning signal
characteristic: What supplies the feedback the learner is trained against.
positive_test: Siblings differ only in where the training signal comes from (labels, the data itself, nothing, environmental reward, a human's behaviour).
negative_test: A node differing in how training is scheduled or split goes to Training regime; a node differing in what machinery computes the answer goes to Inference & optimization.
notes: Fixed by AXES.md s3. Characteristic restated from 'what feedback drives learning' to 'what supplies the signal' so that semi-/weakly-supervised (an amount-of-labelling difference) demotes to depth 3 instead of standing beside reinforcement.

name: Training regime
characteristic: What the training procedure is organised across, or constrained by, beyond a single i.i.d. pass over one dataset.
positive_test: Siblings differ only in which dimension of the training setup is non-trivial: tasks, distributions, time, machines/parties, or an external constraint.
negative_test: A node differing in what feedback drives learning goes to Learning signal; a node differing in what happens to the dataset goes to Data curation & supervision quality.
notes: Fixed by AXES.md s3. AXES's own phrasing ('across tasks, time, agents, data') fuses four principles and collides with Data curation on 'data'; see RATIONALE D3. 'or constrained by' is my extension, needed to give privacy/fairness/safety techniques a Method home (RATIONALE D2).

name: Inference & optimization
characteristic: Which body of computational machinery produces the answer.
positive_test: Siblings differ only in the mathematical apparatus used (continuous programs, discrete programs, probability, causal calculus, equilibria, decision processes, numerical solvers, or a frozen model steered at inference).
negative_test: A node differing in what is proved about learning from samples goes to Learning theory & generalization; a node differing in what structure computes the function goes to Model design & analysis.
notes: Fixed by AXES.md s3. AXES lists 'optimization, combinatorial, stochastic, first-order methods' as one flat child list; stochastic and first-order are kinds of continuous optimization and are demoted to depth 3 here.

name: Model design & analysis
characteristic: What is asked of the model's structure: what it can compute, what it costs, and what can be established about a trained instance of it.
positive_test: Siblings differ only in which question is asked of the structure (what shape it has, what it can represent, what it costs, what it has learned, how it fails, what can be proved of it).
negative_test: A node differing in the feedback used to fit the structure goes to Learning signal; a node differing in the sample-level guarantee goes to Learning theory & generalization.
notes: Fixed by AXES.md s3, but its characteristic is fused: AXES already bolted 'and at what cost' onto it to absorb compression. It has become the aspect for everything about a model that is not its signal or its optimizer. RATIONALE D1 recommends splitting it into Model design / Model analysis / Model transformation.

name: Learning theory & generalization
characteristic: What is established about learning from samples, as opposed to about any one model or algorithm.
positive_test: Siblings differ only in which property of learning is being explained (guarantees from samples, behaviour off-distribution, behaviour on novel combinations, behaviour as scale grows).
negative_test: A node about what a hypothesis class can represent goes to Model design & analysis > Expressive power; a node stating an externally imposed demand goes to the Desired properties axis.
notes: Fixed by AXES.md s3. Small (~65 mentions) and kept: AXES F9 locked the generalization/Desired-properties line here, and theory papers are exactly the ones whose topic vanishes if this node is missing (s5's asymmetry argument).

name: Data curation & supervision quality
characteristic: What operation is applied to the training data itself.
positive_test: Siblings differ only in what is done to the data: perturbed, fabricated, chosen, repaired, or newly collected.
negative_test: A node about what the labels are used as (the learning signal) goes to Learning signal; a node about how training runs are scheduled across tasks or machines goes to Training regime.
notes: Fixed by AXES.md s3 (added by TAIL_VALIDATION F2). AXES estimated ~30 mentions; a full sweep finds ~72, because most data-curation names are singletons.

name: Uninformative method names
positive_test: The name is on the Method axis but names no aspect of method: it would be true of most of the corpus.
negative_test: A name that is not a method at all (Benchmarking, Model Evaluation, Empirical Analysis of Algorithms) is a contribution type and is mark_ignore on every axis, not here.
notes: ADMINISTRATIVE BRANCH, NOT A SEVENTH ASPECT. AXES.md s8b mandates a per-axis uninformative branch but s3 fixes exactly six level-1 aspects and leaves it nowhere to live; that conflict is RATIONALE D5. Reported as a line, excluded from area shares. Holds Machine Learning 250, Deep Learning 233, Neural Networks 19, Artificial Intelligence 15, Predictive Modeling, Optimization Techniques, Algorithms, Methods-Driven Machine Learning.

name: Supervised learning
characteristic: How complete and how direct the provided target labels are.
positive_test: A human-provided target is attached to examples and the model is fit to reproduce it.
negative_test: If the targets are constructed from the input itself, it is Self-supervised learning; if the issue is that the labels are wrong or missing as a dataset defect, it is Data curation > Data quality.
examples: fully supervised classification & regression training; semi-supervised learning; weak & distant supervision
notes: AXES lists 'supervised (10)' and 'semi/weakly-supervised' as siblings. Demoted to one node: they differ in how much labelling, not in what supplies the signal, so as siblings they would break the parent's positive test.

name: Self-supervised learning
characteristic: How the surrogate target is constructed from the unlabelled input.
positive_test: The supervision is manufactured from the data itself by a pretext task, and no human label is consumed.
negative_test: If the point is the pretrain-then-adapt schedule rather than the surrogate target, it is Training regime > Transfer learning; if there is no target at all, it is Unsupervised learning.
examples: contrastive & non-contrastive instance discrimination; masked prediction objectives; multi-view & augmentation-based pretext tasks
notes: Self-Supervised Learning 73 + Contrastive Learning 21. Formally a subtype of unsupervised learning; kept as a sibling because the field treats them as separate programmes. Declared, not hidden.

name: Unsupervised learning
characteristic: What structure in the unlabelled data is recovered.
positive_test: No target of any kind is defined; the only signal is the structure of the data distribution.
negative_test: If a surrogate target is constructed, it is Self-supervised learning; if the name states the required output (a partition, a density, a low-dimensional code), that reading is a Task-axis value and only the fitting procedure stays here.
examples: clustering & mixture models; manifold learning & nonlinear dimensionality reduction; latent-factor identification (ICA, disentanglement)
notes: Homonym declared: Clustering, Density Estimation and Dimensionality Reduction are also Task-axis values (they name what the output must be). The Method reading is the fitting procedure.

name: Reinforcement learning
characteristic: How reward from interaction is converted into a policy.
positive_test: The signal is a scalar reward obtained by acting, and the learner must attribute it to its own actions.
negative_test: If the policy is computed from a known model of the dynamics rather than learned from reward, it is Inference & optimization > Sequential decision-making; if the signal is a demonstration or a ranking, it is Learning from human feedback.
examples: value-based methods & temporal-difference learning; policy-gradient & actor-critic methods; exploration and intrinsic motivation
notes: The largest node on the axis (RL 271, Deep RL 36, MARL 15, model-based 14, offline, hierarchical, safe, distributional, bandits). Per AXES s3 the RL-modifier compounds (Multi-Agent RL, Offline RL, Meta-RL) resolve here rather than to Training regime; see the head-noun precedence rule in RATIONALE D4. Not split by count: conceptual relatedness only.

name: Learning from human feedback
characteristic: In what form a person supplies the behaviour to be matched or ranked.
positive_test: The signal is behaviour shown or judged by a person (or an expert controller), not a label on an input and not an environmental reward.
negative_test: If the person supplies labels for chosen inputs, it is Data curation > Data selection (active learning); if a reward function is given rather than inferred, it is Reinforcement learning.
examples: imitation learning & behavioural cloning; inverse reinforcement learning & reward modelling; preference-based fine-tuning (RLHF, DPO)
notes: MY JUDGEMENT, deviating from AXES s3, which folds imitation (14) into the reinforcement count. Under the parent's characteristic a demonstration is not a reward, and this is the node that will absorb the 2023-2026 preference-optimization literature the 2024 snapshot barely shows (RLHF 2, preference feedback 1).

name: Transfer learning
characteristic: How knowledge fitted on one distribution or task is reused on another.
positive_test: Two distributions or tasks are involved and the second reuses parameters or representations fitted on the first.
negative_test: If no weights change and the model is merely steered, it is Inference & optimization > Inference-time methods; if the second task is learned by learning how to learn, it is Meta-learning; if shift is the object of study rather than a thing to cross, it is Learning theory > Out-of-distribution generalization.
examples: unsupervised domain adaptation; pretrain-then-finetune (incl. parameter-efficient finetuning); sim-to-real and cross-lingual transfer
notes: Transfer Learning 42, Domain Adaptation 7(+2 unsupervised, +1 partial), Sim-to-Real 4, Zero-Shot Learning 5, cross-lingual transfer 3+1+1, PEFT 3. AXES F9 locks Domain Adaptation as a training regime, not a generalization claim.

name: Multi-task learning
characteristic: How several objectives trained at once interact.
positive_test: One model is fitted against two or more objectives simultaneously and the research question is their interaction.
negative_test: If the tasks are seen in sequence and forgetting is the problem, it is Continual learning; if one task is a stepping stone to another, it is Transfer learning.
examples: auxiliary-task training; task weighting & gradient conflict; multi-objective/Pareto training
notes: Multi-Task Learning 19. Kept despite thin corpus: it is the control case that makes Transfer and Continual learning meaningful (same tasks, different temporal structure).

name: Meta-learning
characteristic: Which part of the learning procedure is itself learned.
positive_test: There is an outer loop whose object of optimization is an inner learning procedure.
negative_test: If adaptation is a single finetune on new data, it is Transfer learning; if adaptation happens in the forward pass of a frozen model, it is Inference-time methods.
examples: episodic few-shot meta-learning; learned optimizers & meta-gradients; meta-reinforcement learning
notes: Meta-Learning 26, Few-Shot Learning 16, meta-gradient, hypernetworks. Few-shot is filed here rather than under Transfer because the corpus's few-shot names are episodic-protocol papers; In-Context Learning was moved out to Inference-time methods (no weights change).

name: Continual learning
characteristic: How knowledge is retained as the training distribution changes over time.
positive_test: Tasks or distributions arrive in sequence and retaining earlier competence is the difficulty.
negative_test: If examples arrive one at a time and regret, not forgetting, is the criterion, it is Online learning; if the sequence is a designed ordering intended to help, it is Data curation > Data selection (curriculum).
examples: catastrophic forgetting & rehearsal/replay; class-incremental learning; parameter isolation & architectural expansion
notes: Continual Learning 29, Catastrophic Forgetting 6, Lifelong Learning 5, class/online-incremental variants.

name: Online learning
characteristic: How the model updates under a sequential, possibly adversarial, stream.
positive_test: Examples arrive one at a time, the learner commits before seeing the outcome, and performance is measured as regret against a comparator.
negative_test: If the criterion is forgetting across task boundaries, it is Continual learning; if the regret analysis is the contribution and no stream is processed, it is Learning theory > Statistical learning theory.
examples: regret-minimizing online convex optimization; bandit feedback & exploration-exploitation; performative prediction & feedback loops
notes: BLIND SPOT KEPT. ~11 mentions in a one-year snapshot, but online learning/bandits is a standing COLT-scale area and AXES s3 lists 'online' as a child. Bandit names are mapped here only when the stream is the subject; reward-driven bandit control resolves to Reinforcement learning.

name: Distributed training
characteristic: How a training run is split across machines or data-holding parties.
positive_test: Training happens in more than one place and the research question is communication, aggregation or heterogeneity between the parts.
negative_test: If the question is the convergence rate of the decentralized algorithm as mathematics, it is Inference & optimization > Continuous optimization; if the motivation is that raw data must not leave a party, the privacy constraint is Constrained learning (the two co-occur on federated papers).
examples: federated learning & secure aggregation; decentralized & communication-efficient optimization; data and model parallelism
notes: Federated Learning 24 dominates. Declared homonym: 'Distributed/Decentralized Optimization' reads as either this node or Continuous optimization; the Method surface map resolves it here when the paper trains a model, there when it proves a rate.

name: Constrained learning
characteristic: Which externally imposed requirement the training procedure is made to satisfy.
positive_test: Training is modified so the resulting model provably or measurably satisfies a requirement about its behaviour, at a cost in fit.
negative_test: If the constraint is a structural feature of the optimization problem (a feasible set, a Lagrangian), it is Continuous optimization; if the name states the demand rather than the machinery (Green AI, Trustworthy AI), it is a Desired properties value.
examples: differentially private training; fairness-constrained learning & bias mitigation; safe reinforcement learning
notes: MY JUDGEMENT, and the clearest schema gap I found. AXES s2 rules that efficiency METHODS stay in the Method tree while Frugal AI is the demand, but states that rule only for Frugal AI. Generalized, it demands a Method home for privacy mechanisms (Differential Privacy 8, PPML 4, Privacy in ML 3, unlearning 2), fairness interventions (Bias Mitigation 8, Fairness Algorithms, Fair Classification) and safety constraints (Safe RL, Constrained MDPs) - which AXES provides nowhere. Filed here because all three modify training under a behavioural requirement. It does NOT satisfy the parent's stated characteristic; see RATIONALE D2.

name: Continuous optimization
characteristic: What structure of the continuous objective the method exploits.
positive_test: The decision variables are continuous and the contribution is an algorithm, a rate, or an empirical recipe for minimizing an objective.
negative_test: If the variables are discrete, it is Combinatorial optimization; if the object is a posterior rather than a minimizer, it is Probabilistic inference; if the claim is about generalization rather than convergence, it is Learning theory.
examples: stochastic gradient methods, adaptive steps & variance reduction; convex/non-convex convergence, minimax & bilevel problems; empirical optimization of deep networks (schedules, regularization, sharpness)
notes: Optimization 71 plus ~35 mentions of empirical deep-network training (Neural Network Optimization 8, Optimization in Deep Learning 4, Neural Network Training 6, Training Dynamics, SAM 2, Large Batch Training, Regularization, Loss Functions, Initialization) which AXES gives no home at all. Filed at depth 3 here on the grounds that the machinery is the same first-order stochastic machinery; if a re-extraction grows it, promote it to depth 2. Bayesian/black-box optimization (BO 5, HPO 2, model-based optimization 6, surrogate-based 2) also sits at depth 3 here.

name: Combinatorial optimization
characteristic: How a discrete feasible set is searched or relaxed.
positive_test: The decision variables are discrete or the object is a combinatorial structure (an assignment, a route, a schedule, a satisfying assignment).
negative_test: If the variables are continuous, it is Continuous optimization; if the sector that poses the problem is the point (transport, supply chain), that reading is Application > Industry & commerce and only the machinery stays here.
examples: integer & mixed-integer programming; metaheuristics, evolutionary & local search; learning-augmented solvers (neural combinatorial optimization, SAT with GNNs)
notes: Operations Research 19+1 is filed here by AXES s7's locked ruling ('supplies machinery -> Method'); TAIL_VALIDATION confirms the split on 'Operational Research in Public Transportation'. Also Combinatorial Optimization 17, MIP/MILP/ILP 7, Stochastic Programming 4, metaheuristics/evolutionary 5, constraint & SAT/SMT 4.

name: Probabilistic inference
characteristic: How a distribution over unknowns is represented and computed.
positive_test: The answer is a distribution (a posterior, a predictive interval, a calibrated score), not a point.
negative_test: If the distribution is the thing being sampled from as a generative artefact, it is Model design > Generative model families; if the claim is that the system must know when it is wrong, that demand is a Desired properties value.
examples: variational inference & amortized inference; Markov chain and sequential Monte Carlo; uncertainty quantification, calibration & conformal prediction
notes: Bayesian Inference 19, Uncertainty Estimation 12, probabilistic modelling 17, Monte Carlo 12, Normalizing Flows 5, UQ 5, graphical models 4, simulation-based inference 4, ensembles 9. Uncertainty quantification (~35) was considered as its own depth-2 sibling and merged: it is the applied face of the same machinery. Cross-axis tension declared: 'the model should know what it does not know' is arguably a Trustworthy-AI demand, and AXES s2 does not list calibration among Trustworthy's children.

name: Causal inference
characteristic: Which causal question is answered from which kind of data.
positive_test: The quantity sought is interventional or counterfactual, and identification from the available data is part of the problem.
negative_test: If the contribution is only a correlational predictor on the same data, it is not here; if the graph is a data modality rather than a causal object, that reading is Modality > Graphs.
examples: causal discovery & structure learning; treatment-effect estimation (ATE/CATE); causal representation learning & identifiability
notes: Forced by AXES s3 ('Causal Inference (16) is Method', owner, locked), including the named children causal discovery 6, effect estimation, Causal Representation Learning 8.

name: Game theory
characteristic: How the solution concept for interacting rational agents is computed.
positive_test: The answer is an equilibrium, a mechanism or an allocation among agents with distinct objectives.
negative_test: If the agents learn from reward rather than solve for an equilibrium, it is Learning signal > Reinforcement learning (multi-agent RL); if economics is the field posing the problem, that reading is Application > Social & behavioural sciences.
examples: equilibrium computation & learning in games; mechanism & auction design; cooperative and coalitional games
notes: Game Theory 20, forced by AXES s7. Mechanism design has zero corpus support and is kept as a blind spot: it is half of the field and a single institute-year will not always contain it.

name: Sequential decision-making
characteristic: How a policy is computed from a known model of the dynamics.
positive_test: Dynamics (or a simulator) are given, and the contribution computes or analyses a policy or trajectory without learning the reward from interaction.
negative_test: If the policy is learned from sampled reward, it is Learning signal > Reinforcement learning; if robots are the field posing the problem, that reading is Application > Robotics.
examples: Markov decision processes & dynamic programming; optimal control and model-predictive control; search, motion and task planning
notes: Declared homonym with Application > Robotics ('Control Systems' 9 is filed there by AXES s7 while 'Control Theory' 2 and 'Model Predictive Control' 3 are machinery and are filed here). POMDPs 5, MDPs 3, planning names ~10.

name: Numerical methods
characteristic: How a continuous physical or dynamical system is solved or emulated.
positive_test: The object computed is the solution of a differential, integral or dynamical system, or a learned stand-in for one.
negative_test: If the science that poses the equations is the point, that reading is Application > Physical & environmental sciences; if the network structure is the contribution, it is Model design > Neural architectures.
examples: neural PDE solvers & operator learning; physics-informed and physics-constrained learning; differentiable simulation & surrogate models
notes: BLIND SPOT KEPT AND EXPANDED. AXES names no scientific-computing machinery anywhere. Corpus support is real but scattered (PDEs 3+1, Differential Equations 2, Dynamical Systems 4, PINNs 2, Operator Learning 1, Differentiable Programming 3, Surrogate Modeling 2+1, Optimal Transport 4, interatomic potentials 1). This is the AI-for-science machinery node and is the one most likely to grow by 2026.

name: Inference-time methods
characteristic: How a frozen model is steered or augmented at inference, without changing its parameters.
positive_test: No parameter is updated; the contribution is in the context, the retrieval, the decoding or the amount of computation spent per query.
negative_test: If any weights are updated, however few, it is Training regime > Transfer learning; if the point is that inference is cheaper, it is Model design > Model efficiency techniques.
examples: prompting & in-context adaptation; retrieval-augmented generation & tool use; decoding strategies and test-time search
notes: BLIND SPOT KEPT, AND THE LARGEST HOLE IN AXES.md. The 2024 snapshot gives Prompt Engineering 6, In-Context Learning 4, RAG 1, Tool-Augmented Learning 1, Chain-of-Thought 1 and nothing else, and AXES has no aspect that accepts them: they are not a learning signal, not a training regime and not a model structure. A 2023-2026 re-extraction will make this one of the largest Method nodes. Justified on structure, not on 2024 counts.

name: Neural architectures
characteristic: What computational structure the network imposes on the function.
positive_test: The name picks out how computation is wired (what attends to what, what recurs, what is shared, what is searched over).
negative_test: If the architecture name implies one modality or one task, AXES s5 routes it off this axis (Graph Neural Networks -> Modality > Graphs); if the question is what the class can represent rather than how it is wired, it is Expressive power.
examples: attention & transformer architectures; recurrent and state-space models; neural architecture search
notes: Landing site for AXES s5 row 2 ('implies neither a modality nor a task'): Transformers 13+8+4, Attention Mechanisms 13+2, RNNs 8, CNNs 5, NAS 6 (demoted from a depth-2 child of Model design to depth 3 - at 6 mentions it is a search method over this node's subject, not a sibling of it). Also neuromorphic/reservoir/spiking computing 5, which are a hardware-substrate cluster with no clean home.

name: Generative model families
characteristic: How the family parameterizes and samples a distribution over data.
positive_test: The name identifies a mechanism for fitting and sampling a data distribution (adversarial, latent-variable, score/diffusion, flow, autoregressive, energy-based).
negative_test: If the name states what is to be produced (Image Generation, Molecule Generation, Text Generation), that is a Task-axis value; if the object is a posterior over unknowns rather than data, it is Probabilistic inference.
examples: diffusion & score-based models; variational autoencoders & latent-variable models; adversarial and energy-based models
notes: THE SINGLE LARGEST UNRESOLVED CONTRADICTION IN AXES.md, ~160 mentions hanging on it. s4 rules 'Generative Models (83) stays an architecture' (i.e. Method), while s5's table routes 'Diffusion Models 13 -> Task > Generation' and forbids hedging by mapping to both. Diffusion models ARE generative models. The Frugal precedent (a quantization paper is Method=Quantization AND Desired=Frugal) says the right answer is Method=diffusion AND Task=generation, and that s5's exclusivity rule is the error. Built on that reading; see RATIONALE D6.

name: Expressive power
characteristic: What a hypothesis class can and cannot represent, and under what symmetry.
positive_test: The claim is about the functions a structure can realize, independent of how it is fitted or how much data it sees.
negative_test: If the claim is about what is learned from n samples, it is Learning theory > Statistical learning theory; if the symmetry is exploited to build a network rather than analysed, it is Neural architectures.
examples: universal approximation & depth-width separations; expressivity limits of attention and message passing; infinite-width limits & the neural tangent kernel
notes: Holds AXES s5's 'Deep Learning Theory 7' and 'Geometric Deep Learning 11' plus equivariance/invariance names. Declared boundary defect: AXES files 'Deep Learning Theory' under Model design and 'Machine Learning Theory' under Learning theory, a distinction no annotator will reproduce from the strings alone. The principled line implemented here is class-capacity (this node) vs sample-based guarantee (Learning theory).

name: Model efficiency techniques
characteristic: How a trained model is made smaller, faster or cheaper to run.
positive_test: A model that already works is transformed, at some cost in fidelity, to reduce parameters, precision, latency or energy.
negative_test: If the point is the demand rather than the technique (Green AI, energy & carbon), that is Desired properties > Frugal AI, and the same paper carries both; if less DATA rather than less compute is the saving, it is Data curation > Data selection.
examples: pruning & sparsification; quantization & low-precision inference; knowledge distillation
notes: FORCED by AXES s2 ('Methods stay in the method tree') and s3's ruling that efficiency techniques are a depth-2 family here rather than a sixth aspect; TAIL_VALIDATION F1 flagged the gap. Compression 11, Distillation 9, Pruning 13, Quantization 5, sparsity 5, PEFT and hardware/systems acceleration ~10. ML-systems names (Deep Learning Compilers 2, Model Parallelism, Memory Optimization, Neural Network Acceleration) are only half-served here - see RATIONALE blind spots.

name: Model interpretation
characteristic: How the computation a trained model performs is made legible.
positive_test: The object of study is an existing trained model and the output is an account of what it computes or why it answered as it did.
negative_test: If the name states the demand on the system (Explainable AI as a requirement, Algorithmic Transparency), that reading is Desired properties > Trustworthy AI; the two co-occur exactly as Quantization and Frugal AI do.
examples: feature attribution & saliency methods; mechanistic interpretability & probing; concept-based and inherently interpretable models
notes: MY JUDGEMENT by generalizing the Frugal precedent. AXES s2 lists 'interpretability & explainability' only as a Trustworthy-AI child, leaving ~65 mentions of interpretability METHODOLOGY (Mechanistic Interpretability, probing, attribution, GNN explainers, concept bottlenecks) with no Method home. Explainable AI 10+4+2 is the demand surface; Interpretable ML 9, Model Interpretability 7 are mixed and resolve per-axis.

name: Adversarial machine learning
characteristic: How a model is attacked, and how the attack is defended against.
positive_test: There is an adversary, explicit or worst-case, choosing an input or a training perturbation to make the model fail.
negative_test: If robustness is a demand on the deployed system, that reading is Desired properties > Trustworthy AI > Robustness; if the shift is natural rather than chosen, it is Learning theory > Out-of-distribution generalization; if the defence is a formal proof over all inputs, it is Formal verification.
examples: adversarial examples & attack construction; adversarial training & empirical defences; privacy attacks (membership inference, model stealing, poisoning)
notes: Adversarial ML 13, Adversarial Robustness 10, Model Robustness 7, attacks/defences ~12, ML Security 3, poisoning/stealing/membership inference 3. Same generalization of the Frugal precedent as Model interpretation.

name: Formal verification
characteristic: How a guarantee over all inputs in a region is established for a learned component.
positive_test: The output is a proof or a certificate that holds for every input in a set, not an empirical score on a test set.
negative_test: If the guarantee is probabilistic over a data distribution, it is Learning theory; if the artefact verified is ordinary software, that reading is Application > Computing & software systems.
examples: reachability analysis & certified bounds; SMT/MILP-based network verification; runtime monitoring & safety shields
notes: BLIND SPOT KEPT. Small (Neural Network Verification 5, Formal Methods 3+2, Robustness Verification, Certified Robustness, Theorem Proving 2) but explicitly routed here by AXES s5, and it is the node without which safety-critical ML disappears from the survey.

name: Statistical learning theory
characteristic: What guarantee is proved about learning from a finite sample.
positive_test: The result is a bound, a rate or an impossibility, quantified over samples drawn from a distribution.
negative_test: If the statement is about what the class can represent, it is Model design > Expressive power; if it is about the convergence of an optimizer, it is Continuous optimization.
examples: generalization bounds (PAC, PAC-Bayes, uniform convergence); sample complexity & minimax rates; information-theoretic analysis of learning
notes: Machine Learning Theory 8, Theoretical Machine Learning 5, Statistical Learning Theory 2, Generalization 3, PAC-Bayes, Sample Complexity, Information Theory 3, high-dimensional statistics. 'Model Selection' 4+1 is filed here as a statistical question.

name: Out-of-distribution generalization
characteristic: How performance is characterized when test data is not drawn from the training distribution.
positive_test: Train and test distributions differ and the contribution is a claim about, or a measure of, what survives the difference.
negative_test: If the response to shift is to adapt using target data, it is Training regime > Transfer learning; if it is to abstain on a suspect input, that activity is Task > Detection; if it is a deployment demand, it is Desired properties > Robustness.
examples: domain generalization; subpopulation & worst-group shift; characterizing covariate, label and concept shift
notes: Forced by AXES F9, which splits 'Out-of-Distribution Detection' 12 three ways across axes and keeps only the phenomenon here. OOD Gen 5, Domain Generalization 4.

name: Compositional generalization
characteristic: How competence on seen parts does or does not extend to unseen combinations of them.
positive_test: The test set is built from familiar primitives in unfamiliar combinations, and systematicity is the quantity measured.
negative_test: If the novelty is a shifted distribution of the same kind of example, it is Out-of-distribution generalization; if a compositional structure is built into the model, it is Model design > Neural architectures.
examples: systematic generalization benchmarks; compositionality in emergent communication; length & structural extrapolation
notes: BLIND SPOT KEPT, weakest-supported node on the axis (4 mentions). Named explicitly in AXES s2 as the example that fixes the Desired-properties line ('Nobody outside the field demands compositional generalization'), so deleting it would remove the schema's own worked example.

name: Scaling behaviour
characteristic: How learning outcomes change as data, parameters or compute grow.
positive_test: The independent variable is scale and the claim is about the shape of the resulting curve.
negative_test: If the point is to reach a target quality more cheaply, it is Model design > Model efficiency techniques; if the cost itself is the concern, it is Desired properties > Frugal AI.
examples: neural scaling laws; double descent & overparameterization; emergence of capabilities with scale
notes: BLIND SPOT KEPT. Corpus gives only Scaling Laws 1, Deep Learning Scaling Laws 1, Neural Scaling 1, Language Model Scaling 2 - an institute-year effect, not a field-level absence. AXES s3 names Scaling Laws as a child of this aspect, and AXES s2 assigns scaling to Method rather than to Frugal AI.

name: Data augmentation
characteristic: How existing examples are transformed to enlarge or shape the training set.
positive_test: Real examples are perturbed by label-preserving (or label-mixing) transformations and added to training.
negative_test: If new examples are sampled from a model or a simulator rather than derived from real ones, it is Synthetic data; if the transformations define the supervision itself, it is Learning signal > Self-supervised learning.
examples: input-space augmentation policies; mixup & feature-space augmentation; augmentation views for contrastive pretraining
notes: Data Augmentation 11. AXES s3 explicitly settles this here rather than in Training regime.

name: Synthetic data
characteristic: How training data is fabricated when real data is scarce, private or unlabelled.
positive_test: Training examples are produced by a generator or a simulator and the research question is their usefulness or fidelity as training data.
negative_test: If generating the artefact is the goal, that is Task > Generation plus Model design > Generative model families; if real examples are perturbed, it is Data augmentation.
examples: simulator-generated training corpora; generative-model-based dataset synthesis; privacy-preserving synthetic records
notes: BLIND SPOT KEPT. Seven singletons in 2024 (Synthetic Data, Dataset Generation, Conditional Data Generation, scRNA-seq simulation, ...) and a fast-growing area; kept on structure, not count.

name: Data selection
characteristic: Which subset of available data is used, weighted or ordered, and on what budget.
positive_test: All the data exists; the contribution is choosing what to label, keep, weight or present first.
negative_test: If the data is wrong rather than merely plentiful, it is Data quality; if the selection is a learned inner loop, it is Training regime > Meta-learning.
examples: active learning & labelling budgets; coreset selection & data pruning; curriculum and example ordering
notes: Active Learning 9+1 is filed here, not in Training regime. AXES s3 lists active learning in BOTH rows of its own table (Training regime AND Data curation) - the plainest contradiction in the file; TAIL_VALIDATION F2 leans this way. Curriculum Learning 3 is moved here from Training regime on the same principle (what data, in what order).

name: Data quality
characteristic: How defects in the data or its labels are detected, repaired or tolerated.
positive_test: The data on hand is wrong, noisy, biased or incomplete, and the contribution measures or fixes that.
negative_test: If the contribution is a loss that is robust to noisy labels rather than a repair of the labels, the boundary with Learning signal > Supervised learning is genuinely ambiguous - AXES s3 puts noisy labels here and this map follows it.
examples: learning with noisy labels; data cleaning, deduplication & imputation; dataset auditing & bias measurement
notes: Entirely singletons (Label Cleaning, Data Quality, Data Auditing, Data Imputation, Dataset Bias, Data Poisoning, ...): a genuine research aspect that the count alone would have erased. Declared ambiguity with the loss-robustness reading, per the note above.

name: Dataset construction
characteristic: How a new corpus is collected, annotated and documented.
positive_test: A dataset that did not exist is created, and the protocol for collecting or annotating it is the contribution.
negative_test: If the contribution is running existing methods on an existing dataset to compare them, it is a contribution type (Benchmarking) and is mark_ignore on every axis per AXES s8b.
examples: annotation protocols & crowdsourcing; corpus collection & documentation (datasheets); benchmark dataset design
notes: Sits directly against the s8b mark_ignore rule for contribution-type names, and the line is thin: 'Dataset Evaluation' and 'Synthetic Data Evaluation' are contribution type, 'Dataset Creation' 3 and 'Multilingual Text Corpus Creation' are method. Flagged in RATIONALE.
